name: Symbiosis
oneLine: Two people behave as though together they form one person, each using only part of their ego states - a pairing that's healthy only when it doesn't involve discounting.
whatYouDid: You recognized that Troy supplying all the Parent and Adult while Jules supplied only Child wasn't a sensible division of labor - it was three ego states doing the work of six.
confusion: People assume any close, comfortable dependency is an unhealthy symbiosis; the Schiffs' test is narrower - it's unhealthy only when it involves discounting, which is why a nurse caring for a just-anaesthetized patient is a healthy symbiosis.

fromBook.quote: two or more individuals behave as though between them they form a single person.

expand.definition: In a symbiosis, one person typically excludes Child and runs only Parent and Adult, while the other excludes Parent and Adult and runs only Child; a second-order symbiosis adds a deeper layer, where one partner's early Child needs get met by the other's rudimentary Parent and Adult, making the pairing harder to break.
expand.otherFraming: Competitive symbiosis happens when both people want the same role, such as both insisting on paying the bill or both wanting to be Parent - it's unstable, and typically ends with a storm-off or one person backing down into the complementary role.
expand.tryThisToday: Notice a relationship where you consistently supply the same one or two ego states and the other person supplies the rest - ask what it would take for both of you to use all three.
